title: My Discord game has almost 14,000 creatures, and even I don't know what the next one will look like
author: Faith993
selftext:
I'm a mom with a full-time job, and for the last year I've spent 4 hours every night on one idea: a creature collection game you play without ever leaving Discord. It's called Luna-Bot.ai. Wild creatures (Lunari) spawn while people chat, and you catch, breed, evolve and battle them right in the chat. And every Lunari is unique: no copies, no recolors.

Without generative AI this game couldn't exist. One person can't draw 14,000 creatures. Every day the game grows by up to 100 new ones, rendered on our own server at Hetzner (yes, it's **costly** xD), and that includes redoing the ones that came out wrong. When you breed two Lunari, what hatches can be a species nobody has ever seen, me included.

Players can even design their own Lunari on their own AI platform and post them straight into the game, with their name on them.

What I learned along the way:

Telling the AI what NOT to draw backfires. Writing "no wings" gave me wings. Now I only describe what should be there.

**Keeping 14,000 creatures looking like they belong in the same world is the real work.** I check every batch, and if the same mistake shows up twice, I stop and fix the prompt instead of hoping the next batch is better.

Animation was its own fight. My creatures kept sliding their feet around when they were supposed to stand still and breathe.

*The video shows wild Lunari spawning in the chat, and catching one.*

What's the hardest thing you've had to fight AI on in your own game?

*All art is AI generated.*

[Play free](https://luna-bot.ai)

[Our Discord](https://discord.gg/Ysee67HQkE)

fair point! i'm not checking them alone, i have an art team that helps me look through them and redo the ones that come out wrong (◕‿◕✿)
